meta.title: Discrete-time control: how sampling erodes stability
meta.tools: Exact ZOH discretisation, discrete-time frequency response and closed-loop eigenvalues (NumPy/SciPy)
meta.summary: Implement the same continuous PD design at sampling periods from 1 ms to 200 ms; predict the phase-margin loss from the ZOH's half-sample delay (ω_c·T/2) and find where the discrete loop goes unstable.
meta.problem: A controller that works in continuous time can oscillate when run on a slow microcontroller. How slow is too slow?
meta.theory:
The sample-and-hold behaves like a delay of T/2 (plus the computation delay, here zero): phase loss ≈ ω_c·T/2 radians at crossover. With a continuous phase
margin PM₀, instability is expected when ω_cT/2 ≈ PM₀, i.e. T ≈ 2·PM₀/ω_c.
meta.method:
Plant 1/(s(s+1)), PD controller K(1 + s/2) with K = 4 (ω_c ≈ 2.4 rad/s, PM ≈ 73°) implemented with backward-difference derivative at period T. Discrete PM
from the loop's frequency response on the unit circle; stability from closed-loop eigenvalues.

rows.quantity: T = 50 ms: phase margin ≈ PM₀ − ω_c·T/2
T = 200 ms: phase margin ≈ PM₀ − ω_c·T/2
Sampling period at the stability boundary (≈ 2·PM₀/ω_c)
